insider_note: The one-word answer is sp², but the fullerene cage is only explained once the fourth valence electron is placed, so name where that electron goes as well.

steps.why: The state of hybridisation is read from the number of sigma bonds and lone pairs on the atom. A carbon atom of C₆₀ is joined to three neighbours and carries no lone pair, so three hybrid orbitals are needed and the state is sp².
common_mistakes: Writing sp³. That is the state of carbon in diamond, where each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms.
Counting four sigma bonds on a fullerene carbon atom. There are three sigma bonds; the fourth electron is not in a sigma bond.
steps.memory_tip: Three neighbours, three sigma bonds, so sp² — the same count as in graphite.
steps.margin_note: State sp² and give the count of sigma bonds beside it, so the number is on the page.

lines.text: Carbon in fullerene is sp² hybridised

steps.why: Carbon brings four valence electrons and the sp² state uses only three of them, so the fourth has to be accounted for. It stays in a p orbital and spreads over the cage, and that delocalisation is the reason fullerene is described as aromatic.
common_mistakes: Leaving the fourth electron out. Naming where it goes is what completes the answer.
Writing that the fourth electron forms a fourth sigma bond. It stays in an unhybridised p orbital.
steps.memory_tip: Three electrons go into sigma bonds and the fourth is delocalised over the cage.
steps.margin_note: One closing line naming the delocalised fourth electron completes the answer.
